subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should the default-off admin HTTP RPC plugin reject browser-origin configuration mutations in explicit `gateway.auth.mode="none"` deployments while continuing to permit origin-less trusted host automation?
rationale: The correct rule depends on the intended private-ingress trust contract and compatibility requirements for existing headless callers; source evidence alone does not safely choose that product-security boundary.

options.title: Require private reproduction first
options.body: Test cross-origin browser requests against the real admin route in each auth mode, then add only the protection demonstrated necessary while retaining origin-less authenticated automation.

options.title: Require Origin on all mutations
options.body: Reject missing or unapproved Origin headers for configuration-changing admin HTTP methods, accepting a compatibility break for headless clients unless they gain another explicit bypass contract.

options.title: Confirm private-ingress trust contract
options.body: Treat explicit no-auth private ingress as operator-trusted and close only after a security owner confirms that browsers on the same host/network are intentionally inside that boundary.

recommendation.title: Require private reproduction first
recommendation.body: Test cross-origin browser requests against the real admin route in each auth mode, then add only the protection demonstrated necessary while retaining origin-less authenticated automation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the most directly related shared HTTP Origin-auth seam and documents the intentional origin-less-client behavior.
